LESSON: GUIDED WRITING CLARITY PUNCTUATION GRAMMAR

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing Handwriting Orthography Vocabulary By the end of the 
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is correct punctuation important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use language to convey short written interactive messages
2. construct relatively long simple texts
3. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING CLARITY PUNCTUATION GRAMMAR
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING CLARITY PUNCTUATION GRAMMAR
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use language to convey short written interactive messages

What this means
In this part you learn to use language to convey short written interactive messages. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use language to convey short written interactive messages.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use language to convey short written interactive messages. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct relatively long simple texts

What this means
In this part you learn to construct relatively long simple texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct relatively long simple texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct relatively long simple texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use language to convey short written interactive messages)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar to a partner. (skill: construct relatively long simple texts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use language to convey short written interactive messages.
3. Practise this skill: construct relatively long simple texts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is correct punctuation important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use language to convey short written interactive messages.
5. Be able to: construct relatively long simple texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
